newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends down on hog data, soyoil lower.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends down on hog data, soyoil lower.

text.p: Data from the U.S. Department of Agriculture showing a smaller-than-year-ago hog population caused a moderately lower close in soybean meal futures Monday, CBOT traders said.
On Friday, the U.S. Department of Agriculture said the total number of hogs was 96 percent of year-ago levels, versus the average trade estimate of 98.4 percent.
Soyoil futures also settled lower, under pressure from spillover weakness from soybeans and a late spate of commission house selling, pit traders said.
Sell-stop orders were also triggered near the close.
In late soyoil trade, Refco sold 300 lots March and Cargill Investor Services sold 150 lots March, and commercials were scaled down buyers throughout the session, pit source said.
Soyoil futures were underpinned by market talk that China was still looking to buy more vegetable oil for spot shipment, traders said.
CBOT soymeal settled down $0.900 to $2.40 per ton, with January down $2.40 at $228.50. Soyoil settled down 0.05 to 0.15 cent per pound, with January down 0.15 at 22.71.
In late soymeal trade, Griffin Trading sold 100 lots March and FIMAT futures bought 100 lots January.
Traders were looking for soyoil deliveries to total between 2,000 to 4,000 lots on first notice day Thursday. There are no soymeal deliveries expected, traders said.
Soyoil futures trade was estimated by the CBOT at 14,000 contracts, above the 12,708 traded Friday.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 14,000 contracts, above the 12,748 contracts traded Friday.
